title: High-Risk Medicines: Insulin and Concentrated Electrolytes
subject: Prescription Pearls
preview: Insulin and concentrated potassium are high-alert medicines because dosing or administration errors can cause rapid harm.
quickRevision: Insulin and concentrated potassium are high-alert medicines because dosing or administration errors can cause rapid harm.
Separate concentrated electrolytes from routine ward stock or restrict access according to the safety system.
Monitor glucose and potassium after high-risk administration; investigate mismatches between prescription and administration records.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Insulin and concentrated potassium are high-alert medicines because dosing or administration errors can cause rapid harm.
Use standardized concentrations, clear units, independent checks when policy requires and appropriate administration devices.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Separate concentrated electrolytes from routine ward stock or restrict access according to the safety system.
Monitor glucose and potassium after high-risk administration; investigate mismatches between prescription and administration records.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Insulin units are not milliliters; ambiguous abbreviations can lead to serious errors.
